title: Owner can front-run claim() to redirect entire payment via nudgeSplit (slippage does not cover split distribution)
justification: Privileged-role abuse beyond documented trust scope. The documented owner trust scope covers 'registering strategies, exchange rates, pausing' — the nudge mechanism introduces a NEW unilateral 100% revenue-diversion power not enumerated in those assumptions. Reachability requires a malicious or compromised owner front-running a pending claim with nudgeSplit=100. Classified as Centralization (not Medium) because the exploit fundamentally requires owner malice and the harm is privilege-expansion rather than a state/spec defect — but flagged with strong centralization framing because the new power is novel.
preconditions: Owner is malicious or compromised; mempool visibility of pending claim() useful but not strictly required.
impact: Per-claim revenue grab: claimer pays full amount, NFT burned, strategies drained, but 100% of payment routes to owner-controlled nudge address.
attack_path_summary: 1) Owner watches mempool for pending claim(). 2) Owner front-runs with setNudgeAddress(ownerAddr); setNudgeSplit(100). 3) Claim executes; full payment to owner; phlimbo gets nothing.
centralization_framing: Mitigations (cap nudgeSplit, timelock, per-claim minPhlimboAmount) reduce reliance on owner non-malice and should be considered architectural improvements even if classified as centralization.
